e75e7439-30b7-4f25-b547-f9935b72ae5e.one_liner: Roubini and his partner David Brown argue AI-driven productivity growth will keep real rates elevated but inflation contained, with Treasury supply absorbed by private savings rather than causing a funding crisis — a relevant frame for the long end even though the episode is mostly macro philosophy and equity-options implementation, not money-market plumbing.
e75e7439-30b7-4f25-b547-f9935b72ae5e.recap: Nouriel Roubini (ex-"Dr. Doom," now self-styled "Dr. Boom") and his Boom & Bust partner David Brown discuss how AI-driven technological innovation is, in Roubini's view, a first-order force that outweighs second-order risks like tariffs, geopolitics, and populism. He argues AI could lift US potential growth from ~2% to 4% by decade's end and much higher by 2040-50, funding redistribution to address rising inequality. Brown pushes back, framing the last 40 years as an unprecedented supply-side/low-rate boom now colliding with populism, deglobalization, and fiscal largesse — forces historically associated with structurally higher rates (citing 1970s inflation drivers). On rates specifically, Roubini argues nominal 10-year yields could stay near current levels by 2030, but the composition will shift: lower inflation offset by higher real rates driven by productivity-led growth, not fiscal distress. He dismisses Hank Paulson's "Treasury crisis" warning, arguing US yields are rising because of AI capex-driven private borrowing (a desirable, growth-driven dynamic) rather than inflation or fiscal panic, and that ample global private savings and equity financing will absorb issuance alongside hyperscaler debt-funded capex. He flags Meta's 30-year bonds yielding 7.5% as attractive given the durability of AI infrastructure. The conversation then shifts to David Brown's quantitative approach: using mean-reversion/standard-deviation signals plus Roubini's macro calls to time options (buying puts/gamma ahead of volatility clusters, e.g., February 2020) and portfolio sizing/cash discipline (~50% cash, selective leverage into selloffs).
